answer: Recurring memory-hard puzzles keep fakes scarce. First, each epoch every agent must solve a fresh Argon2 puzzle that ties up 2 GB of RAM. Second, the seed appears only when the epoch opens and proofs are due within ten minutes, so nothing can be precomputed or queued. Third, peers check each proof in milliseconds and drop any identity that misses a round. Keeping 10,000 sybils alive means 20 TB of RAM on standby, roughly $40,000 a month in rented servers. It's like a falcon forced to climb from the canyon floor to the summit every dawn to keep its nest; fat imposters never make it.
